article_title: Multi-source feedback in undergraduate medical education: a pilot study.
citation: Bartman I, St-Onge C, Roy M, Gingerich A, Katsoulas E, Chahine S, Gagnon N. (2025). Multi-source feedback in undergraduate medical education: a pilot study. Canadian Medical Education Journal. https://doi.org/10.36834/cmej.79283
title: R2C2 feedback and coaching model: building relationship, exploring reactions and content, and coaching for performance change
description: The R2C2 model is an evidence- and theory-based facilitated feedback model the article used to train the pilot's facilitators. It structures a one-on-one feedback conversation so that the recipient critically reflects on a performance report and converts that reflection into improvement plans. The article states that 'The R2C2 feedback and coaching model aimed to promote the recipient's critical reflection on their performance report and, through that, identify opportunities for improvement and develop a plan for addressing them.' In the pilot, facilitators trained in R2C2 led minimum 30-minute sessions reviewing each student's individualized MSF report.
requirements: Facilitators must receive training in the R2C2 model
A safe environment for feedback reception, with facilitators who have no influence over the learner's promotion
target_learners: medical trainees receiving multisource feedback reports
examples: Pilot facilitators were faculty members with no influence over clerk promotion, trained in R2C2, and met students for at least 30 minutes
key_sources: Bartman I, St-Onge C, Roy M, Gingerich A, Katsoulas E, Chahine S, Gagnon N. (2025). Multi-source feedback in undergraduate medical education: a pilot study. Canadian Medical Education Journal. https://doi.org/10.36834/cmej.79283

article_title: R2DE: a NLP approach to estimating IRT parameters of newly generated questions
citation: Luca Benedetto, Andrea Cappelli, Roberto Turrin, and Paolo Cremonesi. 2020. R2DE: a NLP approach to estimating IRT parameters of newly generated questions. In Proceedings of the 10th International Conference on Learning Analytics and Knowledge (LAK '20). https://doi.org/10.1145/3375462.3375517
title: R2DE: a regressor estimating IRT difficulty and discrimination of multiple-choice questions from text
description: R2DE (Regressor for Difficulty and Discrimination Estimation) is a model that estimates the two-parameter IRT latent traits of multiple-choice questions from text, addressing the cold-start problem for newly generated items. It builds an input text per question under three encodings (question_only, question_correct, question_full), applies NLP preprocessing and TF-IDF, keeps the NW most frequent keywords, and "contains two regressors that work in parallel to estimate i) the difficulty and ii) the discrimination of multi-choice questions".
requirements: Requires "the text of all the questions and the text of all the possible choices", an indication of the correct choice, and a history of student-item interactions (student id, item id, correctness, timestamp) used to compute the IRT latent traits that serve as training targets
constraints: Model family, encoding and the feature threshold NW are dataset-specific and must be tuned by cross-validation: NW "can be chosen with cross-validation in order to be tuned for a specific dataset"
target_learners: students of an e-learning platform answering multiple-choice assessment questions
target_learning_goals: assessing student knowledge level through calibrated multiple-choice items
estimating the quality (difficulty and discrimination) of newly created assessment questions
examples: Tested against Random Forests, Decision Trees, Support Vector Regression and Linear Regression with five-fold cross validation on Cloud Academy data
key_sources: Luca Benedetto, Andrea Cappelli, Roberto Turrin, and Paolo Cremonesi. 2020. R2DE: a NLP approach to estimating IRT parameters of newly generated questions. In Proceedings of the 10th International Conference on Learning Analytics and Knowledge (LAK '20). https://doi.org/10.1145/3375462.3375517

article_title: R2DE: a NLP approach to estimating IRT parameters of newly generated questions
citation: Luca Benedetto, Andrea Cappelli, Roberto Turrin, and Paolo Cremonesi. 2020. R2DE: a NLP approach to estimating IRT parameters of newly generated questions. In Proceedings of the 10th International Conference on Learning Analytics and Knowledge (LAK '20). https://doi.org/10.1145/3375462.3375517
title: Released R2DE implementation and testing code on GitHub
description: The authors released the code implementing and testing R2DE on GitHub (https://github.com/lucabenedetto/r2de-nlp-to-estimating-irt-parameters), explicitly so that future research "might be run and tested on other datasets". The release is meant to enable a comprehensive comparison with other NLP approaches for estimating latent traits of questions, which was previously impossible because prior works published no code and used private datasets.
requirements: Published so the model can be run and tested on other datasets, enabling comparison between this model and other NLP latent-trait estimation models
constraints: Prior comparison was limited because "an extensive comparison on the same datasets was not possible due to the unavailability of code from previous research and all the datasets being private"
target_learners: researchers and content creators on e-learning platforms
target_learning_goals: reproducing and extending IRT latent-trait estimation from question text
examples: Listed by the authors as contribution iii): "publication of the code used for implementing and testing this model"
